studies.def:
οἰκέτης, -ου, ὁ
(οἰκέω), [in LXX for עֶבֶד ;] 
a house-servant: Luk.16.13, Rom.14.4; pl., Act.10.7, 1Pe.2.18 (In Plat., Hdt., Sir.4.30; 6.11, the pl. includes all the inmates of the house, the familia, οἰκετεία.)†
SYN.. see: διάκονος (AS)

servant, slave; in the NT a person owned as a possession for various lengths of times (Hebrew slaves no more than seven years, Gentile slaves without time limit), of lower social status than free persons or masters; slaves could earn or purchase their freedom 
a male slave, or servant, of various degrees, Mat.8.9, and frequently ; a servitor, person of mean condition, Php.2.7 feminine δούλη, a female slave; a handmaiden, Luk.1.38, 48; Act.2.18 δοῦλος, used figuratively, in a bad sense, one involved in moral or spiritual thraldom, Jhn.8.34; Rom.6.17, 20; 1Co.7.23 2Pe.2.19 in a good sense, a devoted servant or minister, Act.16.17 Rom.1.1 one pledged or bound to serve, 1Co.7.22 2Co.4.5
